quizName: DMV Practice Test #11 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Eye protection:

options.text: Is not needed if your motorcycle has a windshield.
Is only needed when riding in bad weather.
Must give you a clear view to both sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must give you a clear view to both sides.
questions.explanation: California law requires eye and face protection. A face shield protects your face if you crash. Good eye protection must let you see clearly to the left and right.

questions.question: __________ can cause motorcycle collisions.
questions.correctAnswerText: Following too closely
questions.explanation: Following too closely, or tailgating, is a major cause of motorcycle collisions. Always keep a safe distance from the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle
questions.explanation: This sign is on the back of vehicles moving slower than 25 mph. These include construction equipment, farm machinery, and horse-drawn vehicles.

questions.question: When being passed, you should:

options.text: Ride in the left part of the lane.
Ride in the center part of the lane.
Ride in the right part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center part of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center of your lane. Riding on the side near the passing driver increases crash risk. Riding on the far side may cause them to cut back in too soon.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid danger, you should:

options.text: Use only the front brake while swerving.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Do one action first, then the other.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action first, then the other.
questions.explanation: Brake and swerve as separate actions. Do not brake while swerving because this can cause your motorcycle to fall over.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Divided roadway ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns of a divided roadway ahead.

questions.question: Which brake on a motorcycle gives the most stopping power?
questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake
questions.explanation: The front brake provides about three-quarters of your motorcycle's stopping power. Use both brakes together every time you stop.

questions.question: When the lights on this sign are flashing, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Turn around and find another route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with flashing lights, you must stop completely. Wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing before you go. Never try to beat a train across the tracks.

questions.question: The safest part of the lane:
questions.correctAnswerText: Depends on the situation.
questions.explanation: No lane position is always safest. Change where you ride in the lane based on what is happening around you.

questions.question: Experienced riders use SIPDE to make safe choices while riding. What does the "S" stand for?
questions.correctAnswerText: Scan
questions.explanation: SIPDE is a system experienced riders use to make safe choices. It stands for Scan, Identify, Predict, Decide, and Execute.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating you, what should you do?

options.text: Change lanes to let them pass, or slow down to create more space ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes to let them pass, or slow down to create more space ahead.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, ride in a way that lets them pass. Speeding up only makes them tailgate faster, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: What is the best way to stay safe while riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Look far ahead on the road.
Ride faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look far ahead on the road.
questions.explanation: Scan the road far ahead of you to spot dangers early. This gives you time to react to hazards before you reach them.

questions.question: When riding over rough pavement in a work zone, what should you do?

options.text: Look down to see the road surface changes.
Keep your head and eyes up.
Stay on the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your head and eyes up.
questions.explanation: Keep your head and eyes up when riding over rough pavement in a work zone. Ride slowly, keep a steady throttle, and do not fight the handlebars.

questions.question: What happens if you grab the front brake or jam the rear brake?

options.text: It is the best way to stop in an emergency.
It is the best way to slow down on wet streets.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes can lock.
questions.explanation: Grabbing the front brake or jamming the rear brake can cause the brakes to lock. This can cause you to lose control.

questions.question: What should you know about taking over-the-counter medication before riding?

options.text: It is usually fine because over-the-counter medications are not very strong.
It may affect your riding and should be done carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may affect your riding and should be done carefully.
questions.explanation: Many medications, including over-the-counter ones, can affect your ability to safely ride a motorcycle. Always talk to your doctor about how a new medication may affect your riding.

questions.question: If your front tire goes flat, how will steering feel?
questions.correctAnswerText: Heavy.
questions.explanation: If steering suddenly feels heavy, your front tire may be flat. Stop riding and check your tires right away.

questions.question: What should you wear when riding during the day?
questions.correctAnswerText: Clothing with reflective material.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear clothing with reflective material to be more visible, even during daytime. Always wear clothing that covers your arms and legs.

questions.question: Which lane position helps prevent other vehicles from sharing your lane?

options.text: The left portion of the lane.
The center portion of the lane.
The right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Riding in the center of your lane discourages other drivers from squeezing into your lane. When riding behind a car, the center position also puts you in the middle of their rearview mirror, where they are most likely to see you.

questions.question: A motorized scooter can:

options.text: Only be operated during the day.
Be operated without a driver license.
Be operated with any class of driver license.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be operated with any class of driver license.
questions.explanation: In California, a motorized scooter can be operated by anyone with any class of driver license.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. This sign warns that the road ahead becomes slippery when wet.

questions.question: Taking a turn too fast can cause a rider to:

options.text: Drift into another lane of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drift into another lane of traffic.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast can make you drift into another lane or leave the road. Always slow down before turning.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Wear full-fingered gloves.
questions.explanation: Wear full-fingered gloves made of durable material. They give you better grip and protect your hands.

questions.question: Passengers should:

options.text: Hold onto the rider's hips, waist, or belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold onto the rider's hips, waist, or belt.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to hold firmly onto your hips, waist, or belt. They can also use any secure handholds available.

questions.question: When traveling at night, you should:

options.text: Ride at the maximum speed limit.
Be able to stop within the area lit by your headlight.
Ride as fast as everyone else.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be able to stop within the area lit by your headlight.
questions.explanation: Ride at a speed that lets you stop within your headlight's lit area. Slow down when you cannot see well.

questions.question: To properly control a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Allow your feet to hang off the footrests.
Sit so your arms hold up your body.
Keep your knees against the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank.
questions.explanation: Sit with your arms slightly bent. Use your arms to steer, not to hold up your body. Keep your knees against the gas tank to stay balanced during turns.
